subject: history
title: Battle of Hastings Adventure
welcome_lead: It's 14 October 1066. Harold's tired men face William's Normans on a Sussex hill. The future of England hangs in the balance. 🏹
meta_desc: Hastings Adventure — a KS3 walkthrough of the Battle of Hastings 1066 and the Norman victory.
final_note: You saw the fight at Stamford Bridge, the long march south, and how William won at Hastings.

concepts.def: Battle where Harold beat Hardrada, Sept 1066
Battle where William beat Harold, Oct 1066
Long embroidery telling the story of 1066

walkthroughs.body_html:
In September 1066 Harald Hardrada landed in the north with a Viking army.

King Harold marched his men 200 miles in 4 days and surprised the Vikings at Stamford Bridge on 25 September 1066.

The English won — Hardrada was killed. But just three days later, William of Normandy landed on the south coast at Pevensey! ⚔️

Harold's tired army marched another 250 miles south.

On 14 October 1066, the two sides met near Hastings. Harold took the high ground at Senlac Hill.

His foot soldiers locked their shields into a shield wall. William had archers, foot soldiers and — crucially — cavalry on horseback. 🏰

The shield wall held all morning. Then William's men pretended to flee. The English ran after them and broke their wall.

Norman knights cut them down. Harold himself was killed — perhaps by an arrow in the eye, as shown on the Bayeux Tapestry.

On Christmas Day 1066, William was crowned in Westminster Abbey. He is now known as William the Conqueror. 👑

mcqs.q: Why did Britain restrict Commonwealth immigration from 1962?
options: Britain restricted immigration because the Commonwealth ceased to exist in 1962.
Rising public hostility, political pressure, and economic concerns led to the 1962 Commonwealth Immigrants Act introducing voucher controls, followed by tighter restrictions in 1968 and 1971.
Stresemann ruled as dictator from 1923 to 1929.
Britain restricted Commonwealth immigration because there was no work available.

mcqs.q: How did prison purposes change in the 19th century?
options: Victorian prisons were created to rehabilitate prisoners kindly.
Britain restricted immigration because the Commonwealth ceased to exist in 1962.
Prisons shifted from holding before trial or transportation to punishment and reform via the Separate and Silent systems, influenced by Fry and the 1823 and 1865 Prison Acts.
Victorian prisons abolished hard labour and corporal punishment.

mcqs.q: How real was the Weimar 'Golden Age' under Stresemann?
options: Under Stresemann the Weimar Republic was completely stable and prosperous.
Britain restricted immigration because the Commonwealth ceased to exist in 1962.
Stresemann ruled as dictator from 1923 to 1929.
Recovery was real but fragile — funded by short-term US loans that vanished after 1929; political extremism declined but did not disappear; cultural flowering masked unresolved tensions.
